sections.heading: Hold the Line
sections.lead: A survivors game: hold the Eastern Plaguelands against the Scourge for 15 minutes.
lines: Paladin, Mage or Warrior, each with its own spells; blessings and gadgets on level-ups.
Bosses on the clock, coffers with legendary weapons, and the Pale Rider at 15:00.
Talents bought with the gold you bank, achievements and the Argent Dawn's thanks.
A guild board, and a weekly challenge with one seed for everyone. /dz htl opens it.

sections.heading: Naxxramas
sections.lead: Win once and the necropolis opens: four quarters and the Frostwyrm Lair.
lines: Every boss with its own abilities: Heigan's dance, Thaddius's polarity, Frost Breath.
Each quarter has its own floor: webs, plague clouds, rider lanes or slime pools.
Kill the quarter's master to clear it; all four cleared opens the Frostwyrm Lair.
Boss coffers offer a relic for the run; Kel'Thuzad's legendaries after his first fall.
Desecrated tokens make the Tier 3 sets: small bonuses, and the look at nine pieces.
Frozen Runes buy Frost Resistance from Craftsman Wilhelm, against the lair's Chill.

sections.heading: Azeromon: battles you can see
sections.lead: Beasts are pixel art now, battles have a plan, and every move plays its own effect.
lines: Strong moves rest, setup marks pay off in combos, big casts land next turn: guard them.
Six moves per type and each beast's own signatures; a coach helps until your first badge.
Claws rake, waves roll, sawblades grind: every move and every boss cast has an effect.
Taming is a moment: a sigil, an orb that rocks for every check, and a card for your beast.
Every beast is pixel art made from its own model and sized by strength (or keep 3D).
Guildmates no longer vanish at doors or while they fight in WoW.
Sharper trees, ores and props, with real shadows; Stranglethorn is a deeper green.

sections.heading: Every game is its own install
sections.lead: Each game is an addon folder of its own now: keep only the ones you play.
lines: The DisasterZone launcher's Games tab installs and removes them one at a time.
Without the launcher: copy the DisasterZone_<Game> folders you want from the zip.
Updating by hand? Delete the old DisasterZone folder first: the game art moved out.
A game you don't have still has a poster saying how to get it. Progress is kept.

sections.heading: Errors report themselves
sections.lead: When DisasterZone hits a Lua error, a bug report goes to the developer by itself.
lines: DisasterZone's errors no longer show in the game's error window or in BugSack.
It carries the error and what was going on: the page open, your group, your last steps.
Somebody already reported the same error? You're added to theirs as a me too.
Add details on the pop-up opens your report, to say what you were doing.
Settings > Alerts > More options: Report errors by themselves turns it off.

sections.heading: Nameplates while levelling

lines.text: A mob someone outside your group tagged first gets a grey bar: no loot for you.
The level shows in the game's colours: grey, green, yellow, orange or red.

lines: Halo and Slate show the level now too. Settings > Nameplates turns both off.

sections.heading: Recruitment

lines.text: Keep several recruitment messages and swap between them on Message.
Someone who joins through another officer's invite is marked Joined by itself.

lines: Joined the guild on a person's ··· menu marks it by hand, with their team.
Move to another character: an alt who came first hands their story to the main.

sections.heading: Mains for everyone

lines.text: Officers set the main and alts of members who don't run DisasterZone.

lines: Members who run it still pick their own, and their choice wins once they install it.

lines.text: Tanking, you're in your own threat meter: on top while you hold aggro.
Profiles keep the meters' look and setup too, and each character's meter places.

sections.heading: Fixes

lines.text: Fiery Weapon and other procs no longer show the game's placeholder face.

lines: Falling, drowning, lava and fatigue damage each get their own icon.

lines.text: The bag sort moves a few items at a time, so no stack stays stuck and greyed.

changelog.title: Hold the Line, Naxxramas and fixes from the raid

sections.heading: Keys on the next presses
sections.lead: The swing and shot timers show the key each next press is on, like your bars.
lines: The key sits in the corner of the next press and of the presses after it.
The ability's name sits under the ring (Warriors: under the next press).
Read from your own bars: the game's, the Dock, Bartender, Dominos or ElvUI.
Shift, Ctrl and Alt show as S-, C- and A-, mouse buttons as M4 and M5.
Settings > Class tools: switch off the key or the name for each timer.

sections.heading: Timer opacity

lines.text: Swing and shot timers: pick how see-through they are in a fight and at rest.

lines: At rest can hide the timer completely until auto attack starts.

sections.heading: Quiet fights
lines: Every pop-up waits until the fight and the boss encounter are over.
Loot keeps showing straight away. Settings > Alerts > Quiet in combat turns it off.

sections.heading: Fixes

lines.text: Damage meters no longer flip between trash and the boss fight after a kill.
No more error spam from the main tank shield on your own unit frame.
Recruitment no longer errors when a friend's name hasn't loaded yet.

lines: Bingo: plain rezzes after a wipe no longer fill Phoenix Down or Not Dead Yet.
Classic look: the Warrior timer's spell name sits inside its bar again.

changelog.title: Keys on the timers and quiet fights

sections.heading: Azeromon: room at the inn
sections.lead: A full Lion's Pride Inn at night no longer walls you in.
lines: Guests sitting in the inn let you squeeze past their chairs.
Shopkeepers, trainers and people walking about still stand their ground.

sections.heading: Class tools start off
sections.lead: Swing and shot timers, Blessings and Totems are yours to turn on.
lines: Every class tool starts switched off: turn on the ones you want in Settings > Class tools.
After this update they are all off once, even ones you had on: switch yours back on.
Demo mode still shows every tool to try them out.

sections.heading: Smoother logins
lines: Opening the window no longer asks the game for a whole raid's items in the background.
A council member whose guild list loads late now answers everyone who logged in with them.

sections.heading: Recruitment
sections.lead: Guild > Recruitment: the people you talk to about joining, for the GM and officers.
lines: Add someone from a name's right-click menu, from Raids > Guests, or by name.
What they want, their spec, the nights they can raid and their own words.
Fits a team: their nights beside each team's raid nights, and an open place.
Every officer's notes in one story, with their guest raids and milestones.
Follow-ups remind you when they're online: they go on your friends list.
Pass someone to another officer; introductions nobody took remind everyone.
Bring them along: a group invite, a guest seat in a raid, or a member.
Invite: a welcome in guild chat, the officer note, the team's bench, its leaders told.
Then check-ins after a week and a month, level 58 and 70, first raid, gone quiet.

lines.text: Message: build it from your words + helpers (classes a team needs, its nights).
Post to any channel, Say or Yell, each every 30 s or more; a key posts what is due.

lines: Raids > Guests: Recruit now puts the guest in Recruitment (one list, not two).
Every member can introduce a friend from Guild > Members.
The Guild Master sets it up in Settings > Guild > Recruitment.

sections.heading: Walking together in 3D
sections.lead: The others walking in a strategy's room stay where they really are, as themselves.
lines: No more snapping: they run down the steps and stop at walls just as they really do.
Turns, strafing, backing off and jumps show as they happen.
Positions never wait in a queue, so what you see is never seconds old.
Their own race, sex and gear (helm and cloak only when shown).
/dz 3d looks npc: walkers of the other sex as a dressed NPC of their race.
A whole raid can walk together: 25 stay smooth, only the nearest hide behind pillars.
Walking and turning cost far less: a touch coarser while you move, sharp when you stop.

sections.heading: Swing timer (Warriors)
sections.lead: The swing timer's ring for Arms and Fury: both hands and your rage.

lines.text: The main hand on the outer ring, the off hand on an inner ring (gone with a two-hander).

lines: Rage as a globe in the middle; Slate, Pips and Classic show it as a third bar.

lines.text: A Heroic Strike lamp where the swing lands: pulsing = queue it, gold = queued.

lines: The gold line on your rage: queue over it. 40 rage, or 80 for Arms with a two-hander.
Next presses from WoWSims: Bloodthirst, Whirlwind, Mortal Strike, Slam after the swing.
Only what you have: known spells, your stance, Execute under 20%, Rampage when usable.
Every timer theme; Settings > Class tools > Swing timer, /dz war, and demo mode.

sections.heading: A new Atlas
sections.lead: The Atlas is one wide page under a path you click: era, category, place, boss.
lines: Each part of the path is a menu: any raid by phase, any boss by its portrait.
Your recent places sit at the top of that menu, Classic and Heroic ones too.
A raid or dungeon opens on all its loot, one section per boss.
Loot shows as tiles; chips filter weapons, armor, jewelry and tokens.
Search finds places and bosses as well as items, in both eras: try "scar".
Up, Down and Enter walk the results; Shift+Enter adds an item to your BiS list.
Ctrl+F jumps to the search. Click a category's name to see its places as pictures.

sections.heading: Shopping list, by crafter
sections.lead: The shopping list has its own page behind the bag at the Atlas's top right.
lines: One card per crafter, online first, each with its own Whisper button.
The materials sit beside the cards, with the auction house total under them.
+ List on a craft adds it, says who can make it and offers Undo.

sections.heading: Atlas: Classic too
sections.lead: Classic or TBC as the first step of the Atlas's path, for level 1-60 characters.
lines: Classic: Molten Core to Ahn'Qiraj, every old dungeon, professions, factions and sets.
Dungeons are listed in level order, each with its levels beside it.
Below level 58 the Atlas opens on Classic, at the dungeon for your level.
Each side keeps where you were; a search says how many matches the other side has.

sections.heading: Game posters, easier to read
sections.lead: The Games posters say what's yours at a glance.
lines: The label over the painting sits on a dark pill, so it reads on any art.
Your numbers stand out: big figures with a small label under each.
Raid Trainer's times say they are best clears, and mark the boss you played last.
PLAY at the foot of the front poster; side posters keep just your one number.
Between raids Bingo shows your last card faded, with its lines.

sections.heading: A logo for every game
sections.lead: Bingo, Raid Trainer, Chess and Illidan have their own logos, like Azeromon.
lines: The logos stand in for the names on the Games posters.
Illidan's title screen and the Chess lobby open with theirs.
Bingo's logo stands over the card until a game deals you one.
Raid Trainer's briefing card carries it above the boss's name.
